edges.description: W398Ter and Arg513Ter introduce premature termination codons that can trigger transcript surveillance.
Splice-site disruption and other loss-of-function alleles impair functional protein through allele-dependent routes.
Depletion of mature mutant transcript reduces protein production.
Loss of normal pointed-end elongation impairs thin-filament length regulation.
Calcium transients are perturbed after loss of normal LMOD2; intermediate steps are unresolved.
Impaired actin assembly is proposed to increase the soluble actin pool.
Abnormal thin-filament geometry reduces effective actomyosin force generation.
Reduced calcium availability and altered kinetics can contribute to abnormal contraction.
Sustained contractile impairment is associated with ventricular remodeling and dilation.
Severe loss of myocardial force leads to inadequate cardiac output.
Ventricular dilation together with systolic impairment defines the clinical cardiomyopathy.
Pump dysfunction produces the clinical heart-failure syndrome.
G-actin association may limit MRTFB nuclear entry.
Reduced nuclear availability of the SRF cofactor may lower its target-gene program.
Altered expression of muscle and calcium-regulatory genes may compound the primary structural defect.
